description:
FOUND s437 (Fable review) by a #457 breaking-case probe; PRE-EXISTING on the
4356e77 base (base DROPPED the whole statement because of the `)-foo` lexing
#457 fixed; with the statement now running, the bare `-foo` half is visibly
wrong).

REPRODUCERS (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL HEAD):
  sub foo {8} print -foo, "\n";                 perl: -8      PCL: -foo
  sub foo {5} print "a" x 2 . -foo, "\n";       perl: aa-5    PCL: aa-foo
  sub foo {8} my $s = "zz"; print length($s)-foo, " ", -foo, "\n";
                                                perl: -6 -8   PCL: -6 -foo
Inverse (must stay): `print -foo` with NO sub foo declared -> "-foo" in both
(perl's negative-bareword string); `(-foo => 1)`, `$h{-foo}` autoquote (s374,
#234) in both.

WHY: perl's toke.c resolves `-IDENT` as unary minus applied to a CALL when a
sub named IDENT is already DECLARED at that point (otherwise the string
"-IDENT").  PCL's negative-bareword rule has no declared-sub arm.

FIX SHAPE: in the ONE place the `-bareword` string form is decided, consult
`declared_subs` (the same table #413 normalised and the
`_bareword_callable_here` convention reads): declared -> negate the call, else
the string.  Probe the prototype interactions (`sub foo() {8}`; `-foo 1` with
a list-op prototype) against perl before widening.  Filler-sized; low priority
(the shape occurs in no in-repo population as far as the s436 A/B saw).


s439 (Fable review probe): the IMPORTED spelling belongs here too -- `use Math::Trig; printf "%.4f", -pi` prints 0.0000 where perl prints -3.1416 (#365 made `pi` a term after an operator/comma; the `-NAME` site still answers the string).  The fix must ask the one term predicate for declared AND imported `()` subs (Pl::Environment::proto_is_zero_arg on get_prototype).  Acceptance row: the Math::Trig line above + the declared-sub original.
subject: `-NAME` where NAME is a DECLARED sub: perl negates the CALL (`sub foo {8} print -foo` prints -8); PCL answers the string "-foo" -- silent wrong, rare
